note: Everything the kiosk flasher can write. Adding hardware means adding an entry here and dropping the .bin in /sd/fw/ -- no code change anywhere. Keep entries ordered most-common-first; the page renders them in this order.

targets.name: Stump Data Plane
targets.summary: MicroPython for the board that runs the web side. Needs the SPIRAM_OCT build -- the plain ESP32-S3 image boots but never sees the PSRAM this app depends on.
targets.after: Flash the app filesystem next, or finish setup with the Provisioner from the Tools list.
targets.missing_hint: Download the SPIRAM_OCT build from micropython.org and place it in /sd/fw/.

targets.name: Stump app filesystem
targets.summary: The 57 firmware files as a single filesystem image. Writing one binary is far quicker than pushing files one at a time, and cannot half-succeed the way a per-file upload can.
targets.after: Board reboots into the Stump. Set config.py from the Provisioner.
targets.missing_hint: Built on a dev machine with mkfs/littlefs tooling; not yet generated.

targets.name: RNode radio firmware
targets.summary: Turns a Heltec into the Control Plane radio. NOTE: flashing is only half the job -- region, frequency, TX power and EEPROM signing are set by rnodeconf afterwards, and that provisioning is not yet reproducible from the browser.
targets.after: Run rnodeconf from a laptop to set region and radio parameters, then -w STATION for the bridge.
targets.missing_hint: Obtain via rnodeconf --autoinstall on a laptop, or from the RNode_Firmware_CE releases.

chip_notes.esp32s3: Native-USB boards may need BOOT held while connecting. The port disappears and returns under a different name when it enters the bootloader -- reconnect if the browser loses it.
chip_notes.esp32: Classic ESP32 with a CP2102/CH340 bridge; usually connects without touching BOOT.
